newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Higher foreign inflows boost Colombo stocks.
newsitem.headline: Higher foreign inflows boost Colombo stocks.

text.p: A sharp rise in foreign inflows in the first half of this year has boosted Sri Lanka stocks, pushing the all share index to over 800 points for the first time in more than two years, market analysts said on Friday.
Colombo Stock Exchange statistics this week showed net foreign inflows in the January-June period rising to 1.5 billion rupees against 503 million rupees in the same period last year.

"Foreign inflows were mainly to the plantation sector, which foreigners see as being of strategic importance to the economy of Sri Lanka," said Nandakumar Nair, research director of brokerage John Keells Holdings.
Plantations remain the country's largest net foreign exchange earner, with value additions amounting to over 95 percent.
Earnings from plantations, led by tea, are seen rising in 1997 over 1996 due to continuing high demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States and the Middle East.
"But overall, even the other sectors are expected to perform well in 1997 due to lower interest rates and an uninterrupted power supply," Nair added.
Colombo stocks fell to below 600 points in June 1996 for the first time in three years amid gloomy economic forcasts stemming from a crippling drought and long power cuts.
The Colombo Stocks Exchange all share index ended Thursday at 810 points, a rise of 33 percent from 607 points on January 2.
"From a negative growth position in 1996, we have forecast EPS (earnings per share) forecasts of 29 percent for 1997," said Panduka Ambanpola, head of research at brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB.
"And year-to-date, the market has given a return of 27 percent in dollar terms," he added.
The sharp rise in net foreign inlows through the stock exchange has also had an impact on the foreign exchange market, dealers said.

"With the market being well supplied with dollars by way of foreign inflows to the stock market, the exchange rate has hovered near the Central Bank's lower level for the last three weeks," said Wasantha Alutwela, senior corporate dealer at Standard Chartered Bank.
The rupee has stagnated at around 58.48 to the dollar most of this week.
